prompt: Print text containing quotes, tabs and backslashes. Complete printQuote and printWindowsPath using escape sequences.
explanation: Some characters cannot be typed directly inside a string literal because the compiler would read them as the end of the string or as part of the source. The escape sequences cover them: \" for a double quote, \t for a tab and \\ for a single backslash. What the compiler stores is one character per escape, which is why the printed path C:\logs\app.txt contains two backslashes even though the literal shows four.
hints: The first line is just speaker + " said:" -- no escapes needed there.
The second line is a tab, a quote character, the words, and another quote character: "\t\"" + quote + "\"".
For the path, every single backslash you want to print is written as two in the literal: "C:\\" + folder + "\\" + file.
